date_note: Date of the prime minister's statement as reported by VOV on 20 November; the bill's first-reading vote is reported as 17 November.
exec: France is raising security standards for state systems; a bill would extend security obligations to thousands of firms and public bodies.
plain: French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu says the cyber threat is at a particularly serious level and the state will tighten security standards for its information systems.
summary: VOV reports French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said on 19 November the cyber threat is at a particularly serious level and the government will tighten security standards for state information systems. VOV adds that the lower house passed a bill at first reading on 17 November extending security obligations to thousands of firms and public bodies, with more ANSSI powers. ZDNet Korea says Lecornu also called the threat "unprecedented".
title: France to tighten security standards for state systems; cyber bill passes first reading

validation.note: VOV and ZDNet Korea, two independent publishers, each report Lecornu's 19 November statement that the threat is particularly serious and unprecedented and the planned tightening; both relay the press conference, the French government original was not read.

review.note: Compared with VOV and ZDNet Korea: summary cut under 75 words; dropped Strubel title (ZDNet says secretary-general, VOV director general, unresolved); dates, bill scope, ANSSI powers, unprecedented match
